name: Krabi & Railay
tagline: A mainland province of sheer limestone cliffs, a beach reachable only by boat, and some of the best rock climbing on earth rising directly out of the sea.
highlight: The view from Railay's Phra Nang Cave Beach, its sheer limestone cliffs rising straight from turquoise water, no road ever reaching it.
shortDescription: Thailand's most dramatic stretch of limestone coastline, home to Railay's boat-only beaches and world-class rock climbing.
metaDescription: A Krabi and Railay travel guide: the beaches, rock climbing, island-hopping, when to go and a practical three-day itinerary.
knownFor: Limestone cliffs, Railay Beach, rock climbing, island-hopping
goodFor: Scenery, rock climbing, beaches, a quieter alternative to Phuket

image.alt: Railay Beach's limestone cliffs rising from the turquoise water

intro: Krabi province holds some of the most dramatic coastal scenery in Thailand, its sheer limestone karsts rising directly from the Andaman Sea in formations that make the whole region feel different from anywhere else in the country.

The centrepiece is Railay, a small peninsula reachable only by boat, its towering cliffs cutting it off from the mainland road network entirely and creating a singular setting of beaches, jungle and rock that draws climbers from around the world alongside beach-focused visitors.

Beyond Railay, Krabi town serves as the practical gateway to the wider province, with Ao Nang's more developed beach strip, dozens of nearby islands and Phang Nga Bay's karst-studded waters all within easy boat reach, giving the region a genuine range beyond its famous cliffs alone.

whyVisit.intro: Krabi's case is that its limestone scenery is more dramatic than anywhere else on Thailand's Andaman coast, and Railay's isolation keeps it feeling special.

points.title: Railay's isolation is part of the appeal
points.text: Reachable only by boat, its cliffs and beaches feel considerably more remote than the short journey from Krabi town suggests.

points.title: The rock climbing is world-class
points.text: Railay draws climbers internationally for its sheer limestone walls, with routes suited to complete beginners and experts alike.

points.title: The karst scenery outclasses anywhere else on this coast
points.text: Krabi's limestone formations are more concentrated and dramatic than Phuket's comparatively gentler coastline.

points.title: It's a quieter alternative to Phuket
points.text: A smaller-scale, less developed atmosphere while still offering excellent infrastructure and island access.

points.title: Island-hopping is excellent from here too
points.text: The Phi Phi Islands and Phang Nga Bay are both easily reached from Krabi's ports, not just Phuket's.

attractionsIntro: Krabi and Railay's essential sights, centred on the region's dramatic limestone coastline.

attractions.name: Railay Beach (East and West)

image.alt: Railay Beach's limestone cliffs rising from the turquoise water

attractions.text: The peninsula's two main beaches, West Railay's postcard sand and East Railay's mangrove-lined boat pier, both framed by sheer limestone cliffs on every side.
attractions.tip: West Railay is better for swimming and sunset; East Railay is where the boats and most budget accommodation sit.

attractions.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach
attractions.text: Railay's most celebrated beach, a short walk from the main peninsula, home to a shrine where local fishermen leave offerings for a legendary sea princess.
attractions.tip: Visit early morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday crowds that gather at this popular spot.

attractions.name: The Railay viewpoint and lagoon
attractions.text: A strenuous climb via ropes and ladders up a limestone cliff face leads to a hidden lagoon and a sweeping viewpoint over the peninsula.
attractions.tip: Wear proper closed-toe shoes with grip — the climb involves steep, muddy sections in places.

attractions.name: Phang Nga Bay
attractions.text: A dramatic seascape of limestone karst islands, including the famous James Bond Island, reachable by longtail boat from Krabi's piers as well as from Phuket.
attractions.tip: A sea kayak tour into the bay's hidden lagoons offers a more intimate experience than a large tour boat.

attractions.name: The Phi Phi Islands
attractions.text: A stunning day trip of turquoise water and dramatic cliffs, including Maya Bay, reachable from Krabi's ports on a comparable journey time to Phuket.
attractions.tip: An early-departure boat from Krabi reaches Maya Bay before the bulk of Phuket's tour boats arrive.

attractions.name: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea)
attractions.text: A hilltop temple reached by 1,237 steps, its summit offering a sweeping view over Krabi's karst landscape, a worthwhile inland counterpoint to the coastal sights.
attractions.tip: Start the climb early in the morning, both for cooler temperatures and to avoid climbing in the afternoon heat.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the beaches, Krabi and Railay reward rock climbing and boat trips into the surrounding karst landscape.

thingsToDo.title: Try rock climbing at Railay
thingsToDo.text: Railay is one of the world's best rock climbing destinations, with sheer limestone walls and routes suited to complete beginners through experts.
thingsToDo.tip: A half-day introductory course with a local climbing school is an accessible way to try it even with zero prior experience.

thingsToDo.title: Take a longtail boat island-hopping tour
thingsToDo.text: Krabi's four-island tour, covering Poda, Tup, Chicken and Phra Nang islands, is a popular half-day trip combining snorkelling, beaches and karst scenery.
thingsToDo.tip: Book a smaller-group longtail boat tour rather than a large speedboat for a more relaxed pace.

thingsToDo.title: Hike to the Railay lagoon and viewpoint
thingsToDo.text: The climb up ropes and ladders to the hidden lagoon behind Railay is challenging but rewards with a view found nowhere else on the peninsula.
thingsToDo.tip: Go in the dry season — the climb's muddy sections become more difficult after rain.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Emerald Pool and hot springs
thingsToDo.text: A refreshing inland day trip from Krabi town, combining a jungle-set turquoise pool with natural hot springs a short drive away.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit the hot springs first and the Emerald Pool second, since the cooling pool water is more welcome after the warm springs.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Krabi's night market
thingsToDo.text: Krabi town's night market offers a good, low-key introduction to southern Thai street food away from the beach resort strips.
thingsToDo.tip: Try the region's seafood specialties, fresher here than at many beach-town tourist restaurants.

foodIntro: Krabi's food scene leans heavily on fresh Andaman seafood alongside southern Thailand's spicier regional cuisine.

foods.name: Gaeng tai pla
foods.text: A fiery southern Thai curry made with fermented fish innards, chillies and vegetables, considerably spicier and more pungent than central Thai curries.
foods.whereToTry: Local southern Thai restaurants in Krabi town, though be warned it's an intense introduction to the region's heat.

foods.name: Fresh grilled seafood
foods.text: Prawns, squid and whole fish grilled simply and priced by weight, excellent around Krabi and Railay's beachside restaurants.
foods.whereToTry: Beachfront restaurants on Railay West and Ao Nang, where the day's catch is often on direct display.

foods.name: Khao yam
foods.text: A southern Thai rice salad tossed with herbs, dried shrimp, lime and a tangy budu sauce, refreshing in the region's heat.
foods.whereToTry: Local markets and southern Thai restaurants in Krabi town.

foods.name: Roti (sweet or savoury)
foods.text: Crispy pan-fried flatbread, served sweet with condensed milk and banana or savoury alongside a curry, a popular street snack across southern Thailand.
foods.whereToTry: Street carts throughout Krabi town and Ao Nang, several running well into the evening.

foods.name: Fresh coconut water
foods.text: Served straight from the shell, an essential way to rehydrate after a hot day of climbing or beach-hopping.
foods.whereToTry: Beach vendors and roadside stalls throughout the region.

accommodation.intro: Railay's boat-only access and Krabi town's mainland convenience offer different bases for the region.

areas.name: Railay
areas.bestFor: Climbers and those wanting the peninsula's dramatic isolation
areas.text: Accessible only by boat, with accommodation ranging from budget bungalows to upscale resorts, all sharing the same cliff-framed setting.

areas.name: Ao Nang
areas.bestFor: A wider range of restaurants and easier mainland access
areas.text: Krabi's main beach resort strip, with good infrastructure and easy boat connections to Railay and the islands.

areas.name: Krabi Town
areas.bestFor: A more local, less touristy base
areas.text: The provincial capital, offering a lower-key atmosphere with easy access to inland sights like the Emerald Pool.

gettingThere.intro: Krabi International Airport connects to Bangkok directly, with Railay reached onward by a short boat ride.

options.text: Direct flights from [[bangkok|Bangkok]] and several other Thai cities, about 40 minutes from Ao Nang by road.
options.detail: A pre-booked transfer or taxi covers the airport-to-Ao Nang journey.

options.text: Railay has no road access — a short longtail boat from Ao Nang or Krabi town's pier is the only way in.
options.detail: Boats run frequently through the day but stop by early evening — plan your arrival accordingly.

options.text: Regular connections link [[phuket|Phuket]] to Krabi in about 3 hours by road.
options.detail: A private transfer avoids the multiple stops a shared minivan often makes along the way.

gettingAround.intro: Railay itself is entirely walkable, while Ao Nang and Krabi town rely on scooters, taxis and longtail boats.

options.text: Railay's East and West beaches and the viewpoint trail are all reachable on foot, connected by a short path through the peninsula's centre.
options.detail: Wear sturdy shoes for the jungle path between beaches, which can be muddy after rain.

options.text: The main way to reach Railay from the mainland, and to island-hop around Krabi's surrounding waters.
options.detail: Shared longtail boats run fixed routes at set fares — confirm the price before boarding.

options.mode: Scooter or taxi (Ao Nang and Krabi town)
options.text: Useful for reaching inland sights like the Emerald Pool or Tiger Cave Temple from the mainland side.
options.detail: An International Driving Permit and a proper helmet are important on the region's roads.

bestTime.headline: November–April, for the driest Andaman coast weather
bestTime.summary: Krabi and Railay's dry season offers the most reliable weather for climbing and island-hopping, while the monsoon months bring rougher seas.

seasons.text: The most comfortable and reliable weather for climbing, beaches and boat trips, alongside the year's biggest crowds.
Still dry and swimmable, hot but with thinner crowds than the December–January peak.
The Andaman coast's wetter, rougher-sea season — boat trips can be cancelled, and climbing routes can become slick.

bestTime.avoid: Rock climbing on wet limestone during or right after rain — the surface becomes dangerous, and reputable operators will pause sessions accordingly.

itinerary.title: Three to four days in Krabi and Railay
itinerary.intro: Railay's beaches and climbing first, then Krabi's wider island-hopping and inland sights.

days.evening: Sunset from Phra Nang Cave Beach.

days.morning: A half-day introductory rock climbing course.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, timing and transport that make a real difference to a Krabi and Railay trip.
tips: Book Railay accommodation ahead in peak season — the peninsula's boat-only access makes rooms limited.
Pack proper closed-toe shoes if you plan to hike to the Railay lagoon viewpoint — flip-flops aren't enough for the climb.
Avoid climbing on wet limestone — reschedule with your climbing school if it's rained recently.
Confirm longtail boat return times, since services to Railay stop running by early evening.
Book Phi Phi Islands and Phang Nga Bay tours through a reputable operator with a smaller group size where possible.
Pack reef-safe sunscreen for snorkelling around the region's coral.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Krabi and Railay?
faq.a: Three to four. Two covers Railay's beaches and a climbing taster at a rushed pace; four allows island-hopping and an inland day trip without feeling hurried.

faq.q: Do I need climbing experience to try Railay's routes?
faq.a: No — Railay offers beginner-friendly routes and half-day introductory courses with local climbing schools, alongside serious routes for experienced climbers.

faq.q: Is Krabi or Phuket better for a first trip?
faq.a: Krabi and Railay offer more dramatic scenery and a quieter, climbing-focused atmosphere; Phuket offers considerably more infrastructure, nightlife and flight options. Many visitors combine both, since they're only about three hours apart by road.

faq.q: How do I get to Railay?
faq.a: Only by boat — a short longtail boat ride from Ao Nang or Krabi town's pier, since no road reaches the peninsula.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: November to April offers the most reliable dry-season weather for climbing and island-hopping. May to October brings the Andaman coast's rainy season, with rougher seas and wetter climbing conditions.
